question: Should Reef permanently support the Node/PostgreSQL Kubernetes relay as an equal first-party deployment platform alongside Cloudflare?
rationale: The patch adds a database schema, container, Helm chart, deployment documentation, and operational responsibilities that current main does not yet commit to owning; code review cannot determine that long-term support decision.

options.title: Sponsor and harden
options.body: Accept Kubernetes as a first-party relay after the proxy boundary is fixed and live installation, upgrade, delivery, and recovery proof is supplied.

options.title: Split the foundation
options.body: Land a narrowly reviewed shared-core refactor separately, while keeping the Kubernetes adapter pending ownership and operational proof.

options.title: Pause the platform expansion
options.body: Keep Cloudflare as the sole supported relay until a maintainer can own the PostgreSQL and Kubernetes lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and harden
recommendation.body: Accept Kubernetes as a first-party relay after the proxy boundary is fixed and live installation, upgrade, delivery, and recovery proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The current authoritative design records Peter's approval of the existing relay architecture, so steipete is the strongest available owner for expanding that product boundary.
